turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: Morning, Sam. You look like you've seen a ghost.

turns.speaker: Sam
turns.text: Just got the alert from the overnight batch. Customer records are a mess — duplicates, missing fields, some accounts pointing to the wrong addresses. Did you touch the schema last night?

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: Yeah, I ran the migration in the maintenance window. It finished without locking anything, which I thought was a win. But I didn't take a backup first — I figured the window was short and we'd be fine.

turns.speaker: Sam
turns.text: No backup? Priya, that's the first rule. And now the corruption is spreading — I checked the DR site, and the snapshots from last week are showing the same bad data. It's going to take days to repair.

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: Days? That's... worse than I thought. I did take a full snapshot before the migration, but I guess it was already too late — the corruption must have hit the source before the snapshot finished.

turns.speaker: Sam
turns.text: So the snapshot is useless. And you deleted the end-to-end tests to save time, right? I saw the commit.

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: I did. I thought they were overkill for a simple column rename. Clearly I was wrong.

turns.speaker: Sam
turns.text: We'll talk about the policy after we fix this. For now, let's get the restore team on it.

turns.speaker: Sam
turns.text: Good news — the repair scripts finally finished. But the app broke right after the release this morning. Did you see the error rates?

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: Yeah, I saw. The new schema doesn't match what the API expects. I should have kept the end-to-end tests in the pipeline — they would have caught that before we shipped.

turns.speaker: Sam
turns.text: At least you're owning it. But we need to make sure this never happens again. I'm drafting a stricter policy that also covers the deployment window — no schema changes without a verified backup, and tests stay mandatory.

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: Agreed. And I'll add a pre-flight check that validates the backup actually restores, not just that it exists.

turns.speaker: Sam
turns.text: That's a good start. Let's get the policy reviewed by the team tomorrow.

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: Hey, just wanted to update you — I re-ran the migration on a staging copy with the new policy in place. Took a snapshot, verified it, and kept the end-to-end tests in the pipeline.

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: The app stayed healthy after release. No errors, no corruption. The tests caught a minor issue with a date format, but we fixed it before it hit production.

turns.speaker: Sam
turns.text: That's the way it should have been from the start. I'm glad you're taking the stricter policy seriously.

turns.speaker: Priya
turns.text: I learned my lesson the hard way. Never skipping backups or tests again — even if it means the maintenance window runs a little longer.

turns.speaker: Sam
turns.text: Good. Now let's grab coffee and pretend last week didn't happen.
